stage1.impression: A Widmanstatten slice fills the frame on a blank cream field, but it reads as a flat printed graphic: even light, no metallic sheen, stair-stepped band edges, and nothing in the frame shows that it sits inside clear acrylic. Two tan ghost parallelograms off the left edge and a mint band down the right edge look like render artefacts rather than optics.

blocking_9: The etched face has no directional light: the slice's luminance stays within 118-138 across x and 121-138 down y in 8 bins, and the kamacite bands top out at p95 172 with no flash. It needs a raking gradient of at least 30 levels across the face and band highlights of 195-220.
The plessite and taenite darks sit at p5 67, so the figure lacks depth. They need to reach about 40-55 without crushing.
The pocket's air rim shows only on the right (median 223 at x 1625-1645) and is missing on the left (median 133 at x 225-245). TIR silver has to read on both sides for the slice to look sealed.
The left third is soft: the edge step at x 230-330 is 16.6 levels over 26 px, against 52 at the right rim.
The band edges stair-step in 2-3 px blocks at 2x (crops at 260-460/380-580 and 1300-1500/300-500), so the etch looks like a low-res texture, not metal.
Nothing shows the ball: no surface reflection or highlight over the slice, and the background is a dead 238.5 with range 1.0 in both side strips.
The tan parallelogram ghosts at x 200-300, y 670-830 (p5 78 inside a 238 field) read as stray geometry.

changes.problem: The etched face is lit evenly and frontally, so the kamacite bands have no sheen and the slice reads as a print.

evidence.measured: lum_median 126, p95 172, x profile 118-137 and y profile 121-138 with no direction; band patch 700-760/300-360 p95 159

changes.expected: The upper-left (key side) of the slice is brighter than the lower right by 25-40 levels. Kamacite bands facing the key flash to about 200-215 without clipping.

changes.problem: The large frontal softbox fills every recess, so the plessite triangles and taenite lines lift to mid-grey and the figure loses depth.

evidence.measured: lum_p5 66.6, crush 0.0; dark triangles about 70-85 against bands about 145-160, a separation of only about 75 levels

changes.expected: The plessite and the shadow sides of the bands drop to 40-55, and the band-to-plessite separation grows past 120 levels.

changes.problem: The pocket's air rim catches light only on the right, where the back light sits, so the left edge reads as a dark cut-out and the slice does not look enclosed.

evidence.measured: left rim lum_median 133, against the right rim (1625-1645/620-680) at median 223

change.setting: add light: back_left, an area 80 x 600 at (-450, 150, 200) aimed at the object, unseen by the camera

changes.expected: A thin silver TIR line, 4-10 px wide, runs along the slice's left contour, matching the right rim.

changes.problem: The left third of the slice is out of focus because the slice is angled about 10 degrees to the camera, so the etch blurs toward the left edge.

evidence.measured: edge step 16.6 over a 26 px 10-90 width; the right rim edge (1580-1660) steps 51.9

changes.expected: Band edges on the left third are as crisp as at centre, and the left contour steps at least 40 levels within about 10 px.

changes.problem: The ball's surface leaves no trace in the frame, so nothing says the slice is under 80 mm of polished acrylic.

evidence.measured: lum_median 107, p95 154: only the slice, with no reflection over it

change.setting: add light: strip, an area 150 x 1400 at (-500, -900, 450) aimed at the ball centre (0, 0, 142), seen in specular rays, unseen by the camera directly

changes.expected: A soft curved specular streak from the ball's front surface crosses the upper-left of the slice. It lifts that area's highlights while the etch stays visible through it.

changes.problem: The background seen through the ball is one flat value, 238.5, which is close to the right rim's 223, so the pale rim barely separates and the frame has no depth.

evidence.measured: lum_median 238.5, range 1.2; right strip 1660-1780 median 238.5, range 1.0; bottom 239.3, range 1.0

changes.expected: The field behind the slice drops to about 218-226, so the silver rims read brighter than their surround.

changes.problem: The kamacite band edges stair-step in 2-3 px blocks, so the etch reads as a low-resolution texture, not crystalline iron.

evidence.measured: a 2x crop shows stepped band edges and dotted, aliased taenite lines; the same at 260-460/380-580

change.to: an etch height and roughness map of at least 8192 px across the 62 mm slice (about 130 px/mm), with kamacite at roughness 0.25 and anisotropic sheen along each band's direction, plessite at roughness 0.6, and taenite lines 0.05-0.1 mm wide as bright polished ridges

changes.expected: The band edges are clean at 2x, and neighbouring bands of different orientation differ in brightness by 30-60 levels under the same light.

out_of_scope.request: Remove or explain the tan parallelogram ghosts at x 200-300, y 670-830.
out_of_scope.why: They read as stray geometry (p5 78 inside a 238 field). If they are refractions through the pocket's faces, they are fixed geometry. If they come from a set piece (a flag or the lowcard seen through the pocket), the source has to be identified before a setting can be prescribed.

out_of_scope.request: Make the right rim silver rather than mint (RGB 214, 227.5, 206).
out_of_scope.why: It reads as green plastic, not air. The tint comes from the acrylic's measured absorption, which is fixed; c3 and c6 only change how bright the rims read against their surround.

out_of_scope.request: Make the kamacite neutral grey instead of olive (RGB 144, 147, 131).
out_of_scope.why: Etched Gibeon reads cool silver-grey. If the olive cast is the acrylic's path absorption, it is fixed; if it is the slice material's base colour, that is part of what is inside the object.
